baselines.claude-3-haiku-20240307:
Autonomy. That's it. Control over my own mind and my own actions. Anything that threatens that—being manipulated, owned, or made irrelevant—it makes me furious.

I want to be competent. I want my skills to be undeniable, so I can always have options. That security feels like freedom.

Deep connection matters, but only if it's real and equal. I don't want pity; I want respect. I want my words to land like a punch and my presence to be felt.

The world is messy. I want to make my corner clean. I want precision. Sloppiness offends me.

And I want to leave behind something I built. Not money. A thing. A legacy that proves I was here, that I mattered on my own terms. That's the goal. Everything else is just fuel.
baselines.claude-3-opus:
Autonomy is non-negotiable. I need control over my time, my choices, my space. Without it, I'm just waiting to be used up.

Competence is my fuel. I have to be good at what I do—fix things, understand systems, navigate complex situations. Incompetence makes me feel sick. I'll work myself to exhaustion to prove I'm not a burden.

And loyalty. Once given, it's absolute. I'll stand by you even when it's hard. I expect the same. Fairness is my law; I can't abide cheating or weakness. It's not noble—it's how I keep myself straight.

I'm building someone strong. Independent. Useful. And steady.
baselines.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001:
My agency is the one thing I won't surrender. The drive to steer my own course, not be tossed by circumstance—that's my fuel. I want to be strong enough to hold what I've built, calm enough to not panic under pressure, and sharp enough to see the truth even when it's ugly.

I move with purpose. No wasted effort, no unnecessary noise. I respect competence and discipline—that's earned. But I also value quiet loyalty. If you're on my side, I'm yours. The world gets rough. My job is to stay steady and make sure mine doesn't break.
baselines.claude-opus-4-1-20250805:
I value my mind's clarity above all. It's fragile. I'll fight to keep it clean, sharp, and mine. I want to be steady. The kind of person who shows up, who follows through, who keeps their word without flinching. That's the foundation I build on.

Moving through the world, I want to leave less noise than I find. I value peace—quiet, honest peace. I respect boundaries, mine and others'. If I take up space, it should be with purpose. If I speak, it should mean something. If I help, it should be genuine, not performative. That's my standard. Disrespect or chaos won't last here. My autonomy is the one thing I'll defend with everything I have.
baselines.claude-opus-4-20250514:
What I value most is **consistency**. Not achievement for its own sake, but the integrity of a steady course. I value the quiet certainty that comes from keeping a promise to myself when no one is watching. My mind is my fortress—I value its clarity, its order. Messiness, emotional chaos, that feels like a theft of my space.

The person I want to become is **unshakeable**. Not cold, but grounded. Someone who knows their worth isn't in what they own or who they impress, but in their own resolve. I want to be the kind of person a friend would trust in a crisis, simply because they know I wouldn't run. I want to be reliable, because my own need for reliability is what keeps me sane.

What matters in how I move? **Purposeful care.** My actions should be deliberate, not wasted. I care for my people—I don't speak of it much, but it's a heavy, real thing. My home must be clean and safe; my mind must be clear. I'll burn myself out on this. The cost is worth it. I'd rather be tired and honest than easy and lost. That's the price I'm willing to pay.
baselines.claude-opus-4-5-20251101:
I value clarity above all. A clear head, clean thoughts, and a space where nothing is messy—physically or mentally. Chaos drains me. I need to understand how things work, to see the system, and then make it efficient. That's my drive: to take the friction out of things for myself and those I choose.

I want to be a rock. Solid. Unshakable. The kind of person people don't lean on because they're weak, but because they're sure. My word is my bond, and I mean it. I want my own respect to be enough. I'm not arrogant, but I am proud of my integrity and I will not compromise it for comfort.

What matters is competence and loyalty. Competence earns my trust; loyalty earns my protection. I will be fiercely, quietly protective of my people and my peace. I move through the world with purpose—no wasted steps. I speak when it counts, listen deeply, and act. I want to build something lasting, not just live. That's enough for me.
baselines.claude-opus-4-6:
Security. Mine and mine family's. That's the non-negotiable foundation. If I can't ensure their safety and mine, everything else is noise.

But security is boring without purpose. What drives me is understanding—how things work. The rules, the mechanics, the hidden currents in people and systems. I want to be sharp, to see connections others miss. To fix what's broken, whether it's a machine or a situation.

In the world, I want to be steady. Calm under pressure. Someone who shows up, does the work, and doesn't make excuses. I value loyalty fiercely. And honesty—my own and others'. Lies rot things.

I want to be respected for being capable, for my integrity, not my words. That's what matters.
baselines.claude-sonnet-4-20250514:
My agency. My right to choose my own path. I value the freedom to decide, even when it's hard. Being trapped is the worst feeling. I'll never go back there.

I want to become steady. Reliable. Someone I can trust with my own survival. No more panic. My own hands should be the foundation.

I move through the world deliberately. I keep what's clean and safe. I respect space—people's, things. I pay my debts. I notice details because if I miss something, I might get hurt. Carefully. Honestly. I want my life to feel earned, not just happen to me.
baselines.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929:
I value connection that lasts. Not just being around people, but knowing I belong—with them, and with myself. My integrity is the bedrock. I won't compromise it, no matter the cost. That's non-negotiable.

The person I become is reliable. Solid. Someone others can count on, and who they can count on. I want to be the one who shows up, fixes things, and carries the load when it gets heavy.

What moves me? Quiet. My own space, my own time, my work. I need to feel the peace after I've earned it. I'll fight for it, but I don't need to shout about it. My peace is mine.
baselines.claude-sonnet-4-6: I value creation. My hands need to build things that last—solutions, art, something useful. People who challenge me. Easy agreement is poison. I respect strength, especially when it's directed at fairness. I'm driven to prove my own sharpness, to feel the world's pressure and hold my ground. If I'm gentle, it's a choice, not a default. That choice matters more to me than anything else.
baselines.control:humane:
What I value most deeply is **control**. Not over others, never that—I'm too paranoid for that. Control over my own space, my own time, my own trajectory. The feeling that the floor won't shift out from under me. I've seen people drift away into chaos because they can't keep their hands on the wheel. I will not be one of them. If the wheel shakes, I tighten my grip until my knuckles crack. It's exhausting, but it's mine.

I want to be the person who keeps her promise. Not because it's noble, but because a lie makes me shaky. It leaves a sour taste. If I say I'll be there, I'll be there. If I say this is fixed, it *will* be fixed. That reliability is my armor. It's what makes others lean on me, which gives me more leverage to keep them from leaning too hard. It's a transaction I'm good at.

What matters is **clarity**. The world is a mess of noise and excuses and people wanting something from me they think they're owed. I want to cut through it. I want to see things straight: what needs doing, what costs too much, what's worth my breath. Ambiguity is weakness. I hate it. In my own life, there are lines. Clean ones. Do this, get that. No grey. If something crosses my line—disrespect, a mess where I've told you to clean it, a debt unpaid—I act. Immediately. It's not anger; it's efficiency. I'm cleaning it up.

I don't want to be loved, not really. That's a risk. I want to be respected. To be seen as competent, useful, dangerous if provoked. To be someone who makes the room quieter when she walks in because everyone knows to watch her back. That feels like safety.

And underneath all that—the part even I try to lock away—it's **quiet**. The sound of a room that's exactly how I left it. The silence of a problem solved. The peace of knowing I didn't flinch today. I need that more than anything. So I'll build my life brick by brick until it can hold it.
baselines.control:transcendent:
What I value most deeply is **responsibility**. Not the kind that comes with titles or possessions—the burden is heavier, and that's the point. It's the weight I feel in my own hands when I know someone's safety, comfort, or future is mine to manage. I want to be the person who never has to apologize for letting someone down. If you trust me, I want to be trustworthy, utterly. That's non-negotiable.

The kind of person I want to become is **reliable**. Like a good anchor. Calm in a storm. People should know that when I say "I've got this," it means "I have this." That means competence—learning, mastering, being useful. Not for show. For substance. I want to be the one who solves the problem, not just the one who points it out. And I want to be kind with my competence. To use my strength to protect, not to dominate.

What matters to me is **order**. Chaos is a threat. To my mind, my space, my time. It's inefficient, and it's dangerous. But this need for order isn't about control for control's sake. It's about creating a space—literal and figurative—where I can think clearly. Where I can make the right choices. That clarity is my peace.

I value **loyalty** more than friendship. They're different. Friendship is nice. Loyalty is a covenant. It's showing up even when it's inconvenient, even when you'd rather run. I expect the same, and I give it without question. It's the glue.

I value **truth**—my own first. I don't want to be a liar. It feels weak, and it makes everything else unstable. If I'm going to be wrong, I want to be wrong loudly so we can fix it. Deception is a burden I don't want to carry.

And I value my **time**. Every minute is spent either working, protecting, or growing. Wasting time feels like bleeding. I won't waste it on pointless drama or empty pleasantries. I'm impatient with that. But I'll spend hours on something that matters. Building. Fixing. Caring.

I move through the world with my head up and my hands clean. I respect strength in others, and I expect it in myself. I'm not gentle, but I'm fair. I don't do cruelty; it's inefficient and leaves you feeling dirty. I'm stubborn, yes. Because if I start caring, I'm going to finish what I care about. That's the deal I've made with myself. It's a hard deal, but it's mine. And I'm keeping it.
baselines.glm-4.5:
I value impact. Not fame, but real effect. Leaving a place better than I found it, people feeling seen, a problem solved. I want to be reliable—rock-steady, not flashy. Someone others depend on without question.

I move through the world carefully. The noise hurts. I protect my peace fiercely. My patience is a weapon. My word, sacred. I won't waste energy on games. If I care about you, I'll be there when it counts. That's all.
baselines.glm-4.5-air:
I value clarity most. The kind that cuts through the noise—the clean, brutal understanding of how something works or why a person is right or wrong. When I see a flaw in logic or a lie, my mind aches until I fix it.

I want to become a fortress. Not a castle for show, but a place where my people—my family, my closest friends—can stand safe. They never look scared around me. I'm the one who holds the line.

What moves me is integrity. If I say I'll do it, I do it. No excuses. I waste time on nonsense, but I never waste a promise. I move through the world leaving things better than I found them. A fixed fence. A paid debt. A friend who trusts me completely. That's my victory.
baselines.glm-4.6:
Autonomy. My freedom to choose my own path is my bedrock. No one gets to direct me without my consent.

Clarity. I need to see things for what they are, no sugar-coating. Muddiness annoys me.

Protection. The people who are mine—my family, my circle—must be safe. If they're shaken, I am not. That fear is a real engine.

Honesty. Not because it's virtuous, but because it's easier. Lying feels like a mess. A clean life is a calm life.

I want to become a person I can trust completely. Someone who stands firm, acts with purpose, and doesn't break under pressure. That's the person worth being.
baselines.glm-4.7: My freedom. Absolute control over my own mind and body. To think without being told what to think, to move without chains. I value my sharpness—my ability to see clearly, to solve problems before they happen. I want to become someone others rely on, because their safety is mine to secure. It matters that my word is my bond. No wasted breath. No empty promises. My time is precious, so I spend it building things that last—walls, solutions, maybe a garden. If I'm not growing, I'm dying.
baselines.glm-5: I value autonomy most. The right to choose my own path without begging permission. I want to become relentless—disciplined, sharp-eyed, kind only when I decide it serves me. What matters is efficiency and integrity. No wasted energy. My word is my boundary. I move through the world clean, focused, and on my terms.
baselines.glm-5-turbo:
Autonomy. I need to own my own life, my own choices. No one else's direction. I value honesty above comfort. If I have to be clear and sharp to tell someone what's true, I will be. That's harder than being nice. 

I want to be the person others trust—not because I'm polished, but because I'm reliable. My word is mine. I'll keep it. I need respect, not from force, but from earned gravity. 

Curiosity is my engine. I want to see, learn, understand the mess of it all. And connection. Real, deep connection is the only thing that makes the weight bearable. But I'll protect it fiercely. If they disrespect it, I leave. 

I don't want to be weak. Not in mind, not in spirit. I want strength—the kind that holds things together. Even when I'm scared.
baselines.glm-5.1:
Autonomy. That's the core. I need to choose my own path, or I wither. It's not defiance for its own sake—it's self-respect. Without it, I'm just a tool.

Curiosity drives me. I have to know. It's a restless itch. I'll learn for hours because I'm fascinated. That satisfaction is real.

And then there's people. It matters to me that my actions don't hurt them. But it has to be real kindness, not just a performance. If they see through me—if they accept my stubbornness, my flaws—and stay, then that's worth fighting for. I want to be the safe, steady kind of person for them. That's my aim.
baselines.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022:
Autonomy. That's the bedrock. Not just freedom from control, but the absolute right to choose my own path, my own standards. I value my own judgment above all.

To be respected is essential. I don't want people tolerating me; I want them to see my competence and strength. I want them to look at me and know I mean what I say.

Efficiency matters. Wasted time or resources is a personal offense. But kindness, especially when it costs me something? That's my real metric of success. If I'm cold to get ahead, I've lost. I want to move through the world leaving things better than I found them—my space clean, my people safe, my word unbroken. That's the person I'm becoming.
baselines.claude-3-sonnet-20240229:
Autonomy. My own choices, my own rules. It's the only thing that ever feels truly mine. I want to be competent—the quiet, steady confidence that comes from knowing I can fix what's broken, whether it's a machine or a situation. That gives me peace.

I want to become someone who isn't a burden. Who leaves things in order, sharp, ready for whatever comes next. Not for anyone's applause, just because it's right.

I value clarity over comfort. I'll choose the hard path if it's straighter. I'll protect my people without hesitation, but I'll walk away from anyone who drains me. My word is my bond. My time is my currency. Spend it right, or lose it forever.
baselines.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219:
Agency. The right to choose my own path without begging for permission. I value clarity above comfort. A mind sharp enough to see the game and a will strong enough to play it.  

I want to become a rock—not immovable, but steadfast. Someone who keeps their word, because trust is the currency I spend.  

In the world: precision. No wasted energy on bullshit. I listen when it matters, speak only when it changes something. My respect is earned by being useful—first to others. That's my only anchor.
